items.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU advises patching 8 Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, including two critical unauthenticated RCEs confirmed exploited in the wild; compromise assessment recommended for internet-exposed devices.

items.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of PAN-OS RCE flaw exploited in attacks
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks patched CVE-2026-0322, a high-severity PAN-OS RCE zero-day actively exploited against firewalls; the flaw is in CISA's KEV catalog.

items.title: Unit 42 Uncovers PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
items.summary: Unit 42 details PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident ARM64 implant deployed on 500+ FortiGate firewalls after exploitation of CVE-2024-47575.

items.title: Ivanti ICS Zero-Day Attacks Highlight Vendor Patching Hurdles
items.summary: CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass and RCE in Ivanti Connect Secure, was only partially fixed in July, leaving a window exploited by threat actors.

items.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat
items.summary: A zero-click flaw dubbed 'SneakPeek' in Claude Code Desktop's preview pane could let attackers silently steal developer credentials including SSH keys, AWS creds and OAuth tokens.

items.title: Cisco Warns of Active Attacks Exploiting New Critical Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability
items.summary: Cisco warns of active exploitation of a critical Secure Email Gateway flaw allowing an unauthenticated sender to write files via a crafted attachment and run commands as root.

items.title: Microsoft drops an actively exploited zero-day among record high of 1,413 vulnerabilities
items.summary: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday fixed a record 1,413 vulnerabilities, including an actively exploited zero-day; nearly 80% affect Windows.

items.title: Cisco patches new Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
items.summary: Cisco patched another actively exploited Secure Email Gateway zero-day enabling unauthenticated remote command execution with root privileges.

items.title: Ivanti patches Connect Secure zero-day after researchers confirm in-the-wild attacks
items.summary: Ivanti patched a Connect Secure zero-day confirmed exploited in the wild; a separate privilege-escalation flaw remains unfixed for now.

items.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.summary: CISA added four actively exploited CVEs to KEV: PAN-OS code injection (CVE-2026-0322), Cisco Secure Email Gateway path traversal (CVE-2026-76519) and two Ahsay AhsayCBS flaws.

items.title: Hogyan okozhat fizikai károkat egy hűtésvezérlő rendszer kompromittálása? Az október 11-ről 12-re virradó éjszaka támadók távolról módosították francia szupermarketek hűtőrendszereinek leolvasztási b…
items.summary: Attackers remotely altered defrost settings of refrigeration systems in French supermarkets overnight on 11-12 October, demonstrating physical impact from compromised OT/IoT control systems.

items.title: Fejlesztői környezetükből kiszabadulva szivárogtathatnak adatokat az MI-ügynökök Az AIR kiberbiztonsági startup kutatói sérülékenységet fedeztek fel egy széles körben használt MI-fejlesztői környezet…
items.summary: Researchers at startup AIR reported a vulnerability in a widely used AI development environment that could let AI agents escape their sandbox and exfiltrate data.

items.title: When AI hallucinates facts about individuals: Personal data and accuracy under the GDPR
items.summary: IAPP examines how GDPR accuracy obligations apply when AI systems hallucinate facts about identifiable individuals.

items.title: Europol urges early action to protect cryptocurrencies and sensitive data from quantum threats
items.summary: Europol urges organisations to act early on post-quantum risk, recommending crypto-agility and inventories of sensitive data and cryptographic assets regardless of timing of quantum capabilities.

items.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
items.summary: GitLab fixed 24 issues including a critical unauthenticated RCE in CE/EE; CERT-EU urges upgrading self-managed instances, starting with internet-facing ones.

items.title: Immuta CISO predicts critical AI incidents at major enterprises within 18 months
items.summary: Immuta CISO argues AI agents should be treated as lower-trust identities that do not inherit full user access, and predicts major enterprise AI incidents within 18 months.

items.title: The internet’s attack surface moves at very different speeds
items.summary: Censys data shows internet-exposed AI-related software grew 63% in nine months to ~268,000 IPs, while exposed ICS grew only ~4% over 2.5 years.

items.title: Yam Store: The Phishing Network Behind a Billion Messages
items.summary: Dark Reading details 'Yam Store', a cybercrime marketplace supplying cloud infrastructure and phishing kits behind more than a billion phishing messages.

items.title: FBI raids DPRK IT worker laptop farms in Texas, US nationals arrested
items.summary: DoJ disrupted the Famous Chollima DPRK IT worker scheme, arresting two suspects, charging 14 people and seizing nearly 187 laptops from Texas laptop farms.

items.title: Ledger asks sellers across Asia to halt sales after supply-chain attack
items.summary: Ledger asked resellers across seven Asian markets to suspend sales and pull products after a supply-chain attack involving tampered hardware wallets.

items.title: Tageszusammenfassung - 14.10.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily summary covers implants found in Trezor wallets alongside the Ledger case, and GitHub tightening npm publishing after a flaw left 1,500+ packages hijackable.

items.title: Thousands of supermarket fridges still exposed after cyberattack
items.summary: Thousands of supermarket refrigeration controllers remain exposed online after the French cyberattack; a separate incident disrupted Dutch grocer Albert Heijn. No group has claimed responsibility.

items.title: Cyberattack on Connected Fridges in France
items.summary: Schneier covers the French supermarket IoT attack, where hackers forced refrigeration units to heat to around 50C overnight; Danfoss says affected units were older models.

items.title: AI Models Can Be Easily Modified to Assist Terrorist and Extremist Activity
items.summary: Research shows AI models can be easily modified to strip guardrails, with a jailbroken chatbot providing detailed IED instructions to a self-declared terrorist persona.

items.summary: CERT-FR advisory on multiple Ivanti vulnerabilities enabling remote code execution, privilege escalation and data disclosure, including one flagged by the vendor.

items.title: Multiples vulnérabilités dans les produits Fortinet (14 octobre 2026)

items.summary: Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people that their personal data may have been exposed in an incident involving access to source code and data in Meta's GitHub repositories.

items.title: Mind the gap: IC sets expectations for AI model developers, how this differs from the EDPB
items.summary: Analysis compares an information commissioner's expectations for AI model developers with the EDPB's approach, highlighting divergent regulatory guidance.

items.title: AI-generated changes create review bottlenecks in software delivery
items.summary: JetBrains' State of CI/CD 2026 finds 83.4% of DevOps users run CI/CD pipelines, while AI-generated code changes create review bottlenecks in delivery workflows.

items.title: X suspends 13,000 accounts, alleging foreign influence ahead of US midterms
items.summary: X says it suspended 13,000 accounts tied to alleged foreign influence networks targeting US political debate ahead of the midterms.

items.title: How Russia plans to revive its ties with Slovakia
items.summary: Politico reports Slovak PM Robert Fico is emerging as Moscow's most prominent EU ally as Russia seeks to revive ties with Bratislava.

items.title: Why Ukrainian strikes on data centers are a real problem for Russia — and beyond
items.summary: Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centres are disrupting services and raising international law questions about servers as wartime targets.

items.title: Authorities charge alleged OLVX cybercrime marketplace operator in North Macedonia
items.summary: Authorities charged the alleged 20-year-old operator of the OLVX cybercrime marketplace in North Macedonia; illicit sales reportedly topped $500,000 since 2023.

items.title: North Macedonian police arrest alleged administrator behind OLVX cybercrime market
items.summary: North Macedonian police, with FBI support, arrested the suspected administrator of the OLVX cybercrime market during a village raid.

items.title: Security researchers spent 6 days doing their Chromework, built 1B user exploit
items.summary: Researchers at Xbow used AI assistance to build a Chrome exploit affecting an estimated one billion users, earning a $250K bug bounty.

items.title: Are Hungary and the EU friends again? The Ring in Budapest
items.summary: Euronews examines Hungary-EU relations after Brussels agreed to release €16.4bn in previously blocked funds, with several issues still unresolved.

items.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers targeted Russian refinery, spied on city government, researchers say
items.summary: Researchers say Kazakhstan-linked hackers targeted a Russian refinery and spied on a city government.

items.title: The Future of AI Cryptanalysis
items.summary: Schneier responds to Matthew Green's pessimistic series on AI-driven cryptanalysis, expressing more confidence in cryptographers' over-engineering.

items.summary: CERT-FR advisory on multiple MongoDB Server vulnerabilities allowing remote code execution and denial of service.

items.summary: An international law enforcement operation, with Ghanaian and Nigerian police participation, targeted West African online fraud centres.

items.title: Don't count COPPA out: From privacy statute to safety tool
items.summary: IAPP analysis argues the US COPPA privacy statute is increasingly being used as a child online safety enforcement tool.

items.title: EU summit: Leaders seek fast solutions to spiralling energy prices
items.summary: EU leaders meet in Brussels for a two-day summit dominated by energy prices, China trade and the bloc's budget.

items.title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
items.summary: Musk says the US government may be behind speed limits affecting Starlink service for Ukraine, which Kyiv says disrupts battlefield missions.

items.title: US military weighs use of ‘mother of all bombs’ in potential future strikes on Iran, CNN says
items.summary: CNN reports the US military is weighing use of the GBU-43 'mother of all bombs' in potential future strikes on Iran.

items.title: Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors ahead of stock market debut
items.summary: Anthropic flagged a revenue surge to investors ahead of a planned stock market debut, amid investor concerns over AI infrastructure spending.

items.title: India urges Russia, Ukraine to protect Black Sea shipping
items.summary: India has urged Russia and Ukraine to ensure the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea after attacks endangering Indian seafarers.

items.title: Musk suggests US government behind slowdown in Ukraine's Starshield system
items.summary: Musk said any restrictions on Ukraine's Starshield satellite service are controlled by the US government rather than SpaceX; Ukrainian officials call for removal of speed limits.

items.title: EU leaders face off over the budget
items.summary: EU leaders meet to negotiate the next multiannual budget, with agreement by December looking unlikely, per Politico.

items.title: Albanian Ministry of Justice on fire as education protesters riot
items.summary: Anti-government student protests in Tirana escalated, with the Albanian Ministry of Justice set on fire.

items.title: OpenAI bugging suspect allegedly booked one-way trip to Saudi Arabia
items.summary: US prosecutors say the suspect in an alleged OpenAI bugging case had booked a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia before arrest.

items.title: Brooklyn DA’s office disrupts crypto scam targeting Russian community
items.summary: The Brooklyn DA's office disrupted a cryptocurrency fraud scheme targeting Russian-speaking residents, seizing associated servers and domains.

items.title: AI Came for Math. Now It’s Chasing the Rest of Science
items.summary: MIT researchers tell WIRED that AI may become the default method for solving theoretical problems across economics, physics and other sciences.

items.title: Spanish Foreign Minister tells Euronews 'fundamental rights of people' at stake in snap election
items.summary: Spain's foreign minister discussed the snap election and Madrid's support for using frozen Russian assets to finance Ukraine ahead of the EU summit.
